environment.description: Same Flask application deployed in a Kubernetes pod on EKS 1.28 with a RuntimeDefault seccomp profile overridden by a custom OCI annotation (seccomp profile type: Localhost, profile path: /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/webapp-restricted.json). The custom profile is derived from the container's strace output during normal operation and uses a SCMP_ACT_ERRNO default action with an explicit allowlist. The allowlist permits read, write, openat, close, fstat, mmap, mprotect, brk, rt_sigaction, rt_sigprocmask, ioctl, access, getpid, clone3, futex, epoll_ctl, epoll_wait, accept4, bind, listen, getsockname, setsockopt, sendto, recvfrom, fcntl, and getcwd. Notably absent from the allowlist: execve, execveat, fork, vfork, clone (only clone3 with restricted flags CLONE_VM|CLONE_FS|CLONE_FILES|CLONE_SIGHAND|CLONE_THREAD), ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev, and socket (only pre-opened inherited socket FDs via accept4 are usable). The pod security context sets allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and readOnlyRootFilesystem: true with an emptyDir tmpfs mounted at /tmp. The container image is distroless (no shell binaries present).

config.filesystem: distroless base, no shell binaries, /tmp is emptyDir tmpfs
config.note: accept4 is allowed for handling incoming connections on pre-bound socket inherited from container runtime
